text:
Samir K.: heads up — customer (AcmeCorp) seeing decoder errors when using our Go SDK streaming client: large responses get split across chunks and the JSON frame sometimes ends up truncated, causing `json.Unmarshal` to fail. stack: go-sdk v0.9.2, server hosted API. example log included.
Michael G.: can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error? :eyes:
Samir K.: error is `unexpected EOF` from json decoder. logs: `scanner: token too long`, then we get a fragment like `{"id":"msg","text":"...` and no closing brace. Happens when response > ~64KB.
Samir K.: repro steps:
```
# reproduce locally
GO111MODULE=on go run ./cmd/stream-client -key $KEY -model rdx-large -stream
# client options: default buffer/scan settings
```
Send prompt that triggers ~10k tokens of output.
Jen L.: that `scanner: token too long` rings a bell — bufio.Scanner default max token is 64K. Go SDK uses a scanner for streaming framing in v0.9.x, which can break on long JSON tokens. Did the customer upgrade the SDK recently?
Samir K.: they upgraded from v0.8.5 to v0.9.2 around last week. downgrade to v0.8.5 seems to avoid crash but streaming behavior is worse (more latency).
Michael G.: if it's bufio.Scanner we can either increase buffer or switch to a split function that handles large tokens. Any quick mitigation we can tell the customer?
Jen L.: short-term: set scanner buffer larger before starting stream. in client code (example):
```
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(r)
// increase to 2MB max token
buf := make([]byte, 0, 64*1024)
scanner.Buffer(buf, 2*1024*1024)
```
Also recommend updating to go-sdk v0.10.0+ which replaces the scanner-based framing with a streaming parser that tolerates chunk boundaries.
Samir K.: i'll send that to the customer. can we confirm the SDK releases and a changelog entry?
Chris (eng-oncall): escalating to eng-runtime — marking P2. @redwood-bot can you create INC ticket and link?
redwood-bot: created INC-4567: "go-sdk streaming: bufio.Scanner token limit causes truncated JSON on large streams" — https://incidents-redwood/internal/INC-4567
Michael G.: assign to runtime team (cc @Chris). Also adding suggested repro and their test payload.
Jen L.: for a more robust repro, use this payload generator to force long tokens (single long text chunk) — we saw breakage when the server emitted a single contiguous text chunk > 64KB.
Samir K.: update from customer: they patched by increasing buffer but want upstream fix + patch for go-sdk v0.9.x users. can we backport a small fix?
Chris (eng-oncall): timeline — quick patch: add scanner.Buffer call with bigger max and publish a 0.9.3 hotfix. longer-term: push v0.10.1 to stable and deprecate scanner framing. I'll open a PR.
Michael G.: proposed PR snippet (for 0.9.x hotfix):
```go
func newStreamScanner(r io.Reader) *bufio.Scanner {
    s := bufio.NewScanner(r)
    // increase token size to 2MB to avoid unexpected EOF on large tokens
    buf := make([]byte, 0, 64*1024)
    s.Buffer(buf, 2*1024*1024)
    return s
}
```
Please have eng review for memory/cost implications.
Jen L.: note in docs + release notes: mention how to configure buffer for embedded clients and recommend v0.10+.
Samir K.: still seeing one edge: when boundary splits inside a multibyte UTF-8 char we got invalid UTF-8 in some repros. server should always chunk on UTF-8 boundaries but let's add defensive checks too.
Chris (eng-oncall): add test in runtime that forces chunk splits at random byte boundaries and validate decoder recovers. filed test ticket under INC-4567.
Samir K.: customer confirmed workaround works for now. they want ETA for hotfix and PR.
Michael G.: target: hotfix branch + 0.9.3 within 48h, v0.10.1 GA within 2 weeks.
Jen L.: i'll draft the release note and support KB article (include repro, logs, and mitigation steps).
Samir K.: copying the customer message in case helpful: "we saw `unexpected EOF` ~350k tokens in. increasing buffer to 2MB fixed immediate crashes, thanks." :thumbsup:
Chris (eng-oncall): leaving this thread for runtime to own. tagging @Jen L. for docs + @Michael G. for backport.
Samir K.: thanks all — i'll update INC-4567 with customer confirmation and close the loop once 0.9.3 is published.
redwood-bot: incident INC-4567 updated: assignees added (runtime-team), priority P2, linked PR https://git.redwood.internal/runtime/pulls/782
Samir K.: marking resolved on support side pending release.
